Local L128 Continuum Run Bundle
================================

This bundle is a self-contained copy of the K_from_continuum workflow for the
L = 16..128 reference family and the 7x7 test grid used for the large
reference-vs-test comparison.

What is included
----------------
- Spyder entry point:    run_from_spyder.py
- Reference run config: K_from_continuum/configs/local_L128_reference.json
- Test run config:      K_from_continuum/configs/local_L128_tests.json
- Score run config:     K_from_continuum/configs/local_L128_score.json
- One-step wrappers:
  - setup_local_env.sh
  - run_reference_L128.sh
  - run_tests_L128.sh
  - run_score_L128.sh
  - run_all_L128.sh
  - make_large_comparison_plots.sh

Prerequisites
-------------
You need these tools on the local machine:
- bash
- python3
- a C++ compiler: g++, c++, or cl

Notes:
- For the Spyder launcher, make is optional. If make is missing, the launcher
  will compile the simulator directly with g++, c++, or cl.
- On Windows, cl usually means the Microsoft C++ Build Tools are installed and
  available on PATH.
- The shell wrappers still expect bash and make, so on Windows the recommended
  entry point is run_from_spyder.py.

Spyder quick start
------------------
1. Unzip this folder.
2. Open run_from_spyder.py in Spyder.
3. At the top of the file, set:
  MODE = "all"
   or choose one of:
  "reference", "tests", "score", "plots", "all"
4. Press Run.

The launcher uses Spyder's current Python interpreter, installs the Python
requirements into that interpreter when AUTO_INSTALL_PYTHON_DEPS = True, builds
the simulator with make, and then runs the selected workflow step(s).

Terminal quick start
--------------------
If you prefer the terminal wrappers instead of Spyder, run:
  bash run_all_L128.sh

One-command run
---------------
For Spyder, set MODE = "all" in run_from_spyder.py and press Run.

For a terminal run, use:
  bash run_all_L128.sh

Resume behavior
---------------
The configs ship with "resume": true, so re-running the same wrapper will pick
up where it left off instead of restarting from zero.

Main output locations
---------------------
Reference outputs:
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_reference_L128/reference_data/

Test outputs:
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_tests_L128_grid7x7/test_data/

Score and comparison outputs:
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_score_L128_grid7x7/comparison_analysis_data/

Large comparison plots
----------------------
From Spyder, regenerate the large comparison plots by setting:
  MODE = "plots"
and running run_from_spyder.py again.

From a terminal, you can also run:
  bash make_large_comparison_plots.sh

That regenerates the score step and writes the main plots here:
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_score_L128_grid7x7/comparison_analysis_data/score_heatmap.png
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_score_L128_grid7x7/comparison_analysis_data/zscore_heatmap.png
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_score_L128_grid7x7/comparison_analysis_data/score_zscore_heatmaps.png
  K_from_continuum/results/local_iso111_ref4x_qtr_score_L128_grid7x7/comparison_analysis_data/fss_plots/

If you want Spyder to pop open the three main heatmaps after scoring, set:
  SHOW_COMPARISON_PLOTS = True
in run_from_spyder.py before running MODE = "score", MODE = "plots", or
MODE = "all".

What the plots mean
-------------------
- score_heatmap.png: scalar score over the full 7x7 coupling grid
- zscore_heatmap.png: RMS z-score over the same grid
- score_zscore_heatmaps.png: both heatmaps side by side
- fss_plots/: per-point finite-size scaling plots comparing test and reference
  channels plus their continuum fits

Runtime note
------------
At the settings shipped here, the large 7x7 test sweep to L = 128 is roughly a
12 to 18 hour job on 2 workers, with about 15 hours as a reasonable central
estimate. The score/plot step is much smaller than the Monte Carlo generation.

Tuning parallelism
------------------
To use more or fewer workers, edit:
  K_from_continuum/configs/local_L128_tests.json
and change:
  execution.n_workers

The default is 2.
